claim: Softmax activations exhibit high cross-layer similarity in the top half layers of pre-trained LLMs during post-training, indicating redundancy.
falsifier: Compute cross-layer cosine similarity of Softmax activations for top half layers in a pre-trained LLM during post-training on a held-out dataset; expect high similarity values.

exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported LLMs, datasets, and post-training settings; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Layer depth–High cross-layer similarity principle

claim: Under the finiteness condition FC and the constructibility condition CC, there exists a decision problem D_k in the family D such that D_k is in NP and no sound, constructible theory represented in G proves D_k is in P.
falsifier: One can test the theorem by instantiating a concrete family D satisfying FC and a class G satisfying CC, then checking whether the constructed D_k is in NP and whether sound constructible theories in G fail to prove D_k in P.

conditions: FC holds for the family D
CC holds for theories represented in G
exclusions: The result is stated within the formal framework G and for constructible sound theories; it does not assert unprovability in all formal systems.

title: Family of decision problems–existence of k theorem

claim: The configuration space of Wang tiling problems can be partitioned into at least two distinct regimes: a tractable regime where asymptotic behavior is predictable and computationally accessible, and a chaotically hard regime where heuristic strategies fail.
falsifier: For a candidate Wang tiling alphabet, compute τ and analyze the map fΓ(z); if τ is high and the map is non-chaotic, the alphabet should belong to the tractable regime; if τ is low and the map is chaotic, it should belong to the hard regime.

conditions: the alphabet's τ value and the behavior of the map fΓ(z) determine the regime
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported Wang tiling system, the specific alphabets tested, and the simulation conditions; transfer beyond these is unestablished.

title: Alphabet properties–partition into tractable regime principle
